what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1971?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1971 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (136 pages) was searched for wage, gross, salary and payroll and found only aggregates (the accountant's wage lines in the schedule, p53-61, `Payroll Deductions` p44, p50), the Personnel Board's rules (p69) and the School Personnel Listing (p101-114), which names staff, education and years of experience and prints no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1971/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1971 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1971?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1971 report records only the vote on it (Article 3, March 6, 1971: the Classification and Salary Schedule `voted on March 7, 1970` amended by the Personnel Board's proposal, text on p68; summarised on p14-15) and not the schedule; searched for classification, salary schedule, grade and step (sources/data/report-tables/1971/). — closes: the Personnel Board's Classification and Salary Schedule dated March 6, 1971.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1971, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1971 report prints the revolving funds' YEAR-END balances only, as lines of the balance sheet (p40 `Revolving Funds`: School Lunch 2,038.23, School Athletics 263.21), the school lunch and athletic accounts inside the School Department's own reports (p127, p132) and revenue lines in the Treasurer's receipts (p46); no town-wide receipts-and-disbursements schedule by fund. Searched special revenue and revolving: the only hit is p40 (sources/data/report-tables/1971/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1971 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in 1971?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1971 report prints no such schedule: the accountant's schedule lists each special article with its balance (p54-62), the balance sheet carries the unexpended appropriation balances (p40-41), and no capital plan is printed; so whether any project sat in a separate fund is not shown. Searched capital project, capital plan and capital improvement: no hit (sources/data/report-tables/1971/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1971 capital projects fund ledger.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1971?
why: `report-valuation` holds the valuation and levy history from the 1987-2010 reports. The 1971 report prints the assessed valuation as two lines of the opening facts page (p2: real estate $49,009,830, personal property $2,169,120, tax rate $42.50), and the Assessors' prose on the tax rate rising from $33.00 to $42.50 (p7), and no recapitulation of the levy, the overlay or growth. The overlay appears only as a reserve and a funding source (p41, p69-70). Searched valuation, overlay, tax rate, levy and growth (sources/data/report-tables/1971/). — closes: the Assessors' 1971 tax rate recapitulation (the Tax Recap sheet filed with the State).

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1971, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and `sealing-fee-schedule` the fee per device from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1971 report gives the year's totals in prose on p34 (130 devices inspected, 126 found correct and sealed, two pumps and two scales condemned) and the Treasurer's receipts one line, `Inspector of Weights & Measures` $337.10 (p45), with no count or fee by device type. Searched weights and measures, sealer, sealing (sources/data/report-tables/1971/). — closes: the Inspector of Weights and Measures' 1971 test and fee record.
